title: Temple Ordinances Unite, Connect, and Seal
author: Amy Harris

The records for these baptisms do not have a specific date attached, but they likely took place in fall 1840 or early spring 1841.
SeeSaints: The Story of the Church of Jesus Christ in the Latter Days, vol. 1,The Standard of Truth, 1815–1846(2018), 421–22.
See Church History Topics, “Baptism for the Dead,” Gospel Library.

See Betsy Ducett [Duzette] baptisms for deceased relatives, c.1840, in “Nauvoo Baptisms for the Dead in Mississippi River (Sept. 1840–Nov. 1841),” image 76 of 102, FamilySearch.org. Joseph Smith first preached about baptism for the dead in August 1840 (see Simon Baker, statement, inJournal History of The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints, Aug. 15, 1840, catalog.ChurchofJesusChrist.org; see also Joseph Smith, “Letter to Quorum of the Twelve, 15 December 1840,” 6, josephsmithpapers.org).
See Lisa Wilson,A History of Stepfamilies in Early America(2014), 2–3.

The unfolding Restoration would eventually make clear that the welding link includes not only baptism but also other essential priesthood ordinances that link generations (see D. Todd Christofferson, “The Sealing Power,”Liahona, Nov. 2023, 21).
See Joseph Smith, “Discourse, 9 April 1842, as Reported by Wilford Woodruff,” 144, josephsmithpapers.org.
See Russell M. Nelson, “Generations Linked in Love,”Liahona, May 2010, 92.
